name: Rapaso Do Aire
body:
Rapaso Do Aire
CR 5

This translucent silver fox bears the scars of a withered corpse, with ragged rents in its spectral hide and pale ghostly fires leaking out of its ravaged flesh.

XP 1,600
NE Medium undead (incorporeal)
Init +10; Senses darkvision 60 ft., fearsense 60 ft.; Perception +12

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 18, flat-footed 12 (+2 defelection, +6 Dex)
hp 39 (6d8+12)
Fort +4, Ref +8, Will +8
Defensive Abilities incorporeal; Immune undead traits

OFFENSE

Speed fly 50 ft. (perfect)
Melee incorporeal touch +10 (2d6 negative energy damage plus 3d6 fire)
Special Attacks frightening cacophony (DC 15), horrible howl (DC 15)

STATISTICS

Str —, Dex 22, Con —, Int 14, Wis 16, Cha 15
Base Atk +4; CMB +10; CMD 22
Feats Combat Reflexes, Improved Initiative
Skills Fly +23, Intimidate +11, Perception +12, Stealth +15
Languages Common plus any languages it knew during life

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Fearsense (Su)

A rapaso do aire can sense the presence of any creature affected by a fear condition (shaken, frightened or panicked) or affected by an ability that is a fear effect. The rapaso do aire also knows what kind of fear the creature is experiencing, within its range.

Frightening Cacophony (Su)

As a standard action, a rapaso do aire produces disturbing noises, heralding the death of all that hear it. All living creatures within 30 feet must attempt a DC 15 Will save. A failed save leaves the target frightened for 1d4 rounds. On a successful saving throw, the target is shaken for 1 round and is immune to this ability for 24 hours. If a creature fails a saving throw against frightening cacophony while frightened, the creature becomes panicked for 1 minute and must flee for 1 round. The DC is Charisma-based.

Horrible Howl (Su)

As a full-round action a rappose do aire release an unearly howl. All living creatures within 15 feet must attempt a DC 15 Fortitude save or take 3d6 negative energy damage.

Creatures that successfully save take half damage. Creatures that are frightened or panicked double the damage taken. Once used, the raposa do aire cannot do so again for 1d4 rounds.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair, gang (3–6), or pack (7–12)
Treasure none

Spirits of those who committed terrible crimes to prolong their own lives, in death these dark souls become raposa do aire, doomed to wander the land seeking out death and despair, feeding on it to prolong their miserable undead existence rather than face final death. The raposa do aire feeds on the fear of living mortals as well as the energy of dying souls released from their mortal coils.

Raposa do aire are naturally invisible and rarely reveal their true form. When one is seen, its body appears as a tattered skin or fur, whipping and lashing in an unfelt gale.

Atop this form is a vulpine head, with an unholy fire burning in its eyes and mouth.

A rapaso do aire usually keeps itself hidden but manifests to other senses. It often comes in the form of a roar, a moan, or a shuddering howl that runs through every corner of the house inhabited by the person who is about to die. Nothing can be seen, but a definite, hostile presence can be felt, making the air around feel heavy and oppressive. It can be heard in the night, in the air, on the ground and even within oneself and sounds like the sound of cats, crows, roosters and even the cries of children calling to the living. When the scream sounds, those who hear often feel that they are already dead.
